newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar corrects lower, holds most gains.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar corrects lower, holds most gains.

text.p: White sugar futures corrected lower as the nearby arbitrage attracted commission house selling but concerns of seasonal tightness underpinned prices, traders said on Thursday.
Both the whites and raws markets moved lower as profits were taken after the recent build-up of fund long positions in the nearby months.
In London, traders reported scale-sell orders in place on August/July and a slight narrowing of London's August/October spread to around $9.00.
With mixed buying supporting the market at the lower end of the ranges, movements were relatively tight.
"It's a pure correction," said one trader.
Uncovered and open August positions declined as of close of trading on Wednesday as spot positions were rolled into October and other further forward months.
Open and uncovered positions both increased in October and December.
At 1550 GMT August was down $1.60 at $326.80, about a dollar off the day's low. October was down $1.70 at $317.50 and volume reached 1,735 lots, lower than in recent days.
Technical analysts said while August could see a $5 downward correction, the market's medium-term uptrend would probably be sustained.
Resistance was pegged at this week's high of $330.80 with the main objective at $341.00.
In other news, Ukraine's Agriculture Minister said Russian President Boris Yeltsin had promised to repeal a 20 percent value-added tax on Ukrainian imported sugar.
Russia also planned to invest heavily in Ukraine's ageing sugar refineries, he said, adding that the Russians had calculated they would become co-owners in 170 out of Ukraine's 192 sugar refineries.
Paris volume reached 1,174 lots, mostly in the spot month. August was down $2.10 at $326.40 and October down $2.00 at $317.50.
